textbookText: 33. How can the light dispersed by a prism be converted back into white light? Ans:- The light dispersed by a prism can be converted back into white light by passing it through a second prism placed in the opposite direction, which bends the colors back together. This recombination of the constituent colors restores the original white light. 34. White any two problems that may be seen in corneal injury.

Ans:- Two problems that may be seen in a corneal injury are blurred vision, due to damage to the transparent cornea affecting light refraction, and pain or sensitivity to light, caused by irritation of the corneal nerves.

35. The given figure shows the dispersion of a light ray through a triangular prism. Answers the following questions based on the given ray diagram. i) Which colours of light waves are indicated by X and Y? Ans:- X = Violet light (bent the most) and Y = Red light (bent the least) ii) Write down the reason why Y is bent less than X when the light rays come out of the prism. Ans:- Red light (Y) has a longer wavelength and therefore lower refractive index in glass, so it is deviated less than violet light (X), which has a shorter wavelength and a higher refractive index, causing greater bending. 36. Explain the role of the ciliary muscle in the change in the thickness of the eye lens when a student siting in a classroom shifts his/her eyes from the letters written on the whiteboard to a distant object seen out the window. Ans:- When the student shifts their eyes from the nearby letters on the whiteboard to a distant object outside the window, the ciliary muscles relax. As the ciliary muscles relax, the suspensory ligaments become taut, which pulls the eye lens and makes it thinner. This reduction in thickness decreases the lens's focal power, allowing the eye to clearly focus light coming from the distant object. 37. Explain, with a ray diagram, the role of the lens used to correct long-sightedness. Ans:- Long-sightedness is corrected using a convex lens, which converges the light rays coming from a nearby object before they enter the eye. Because the unaided eye forms the image behind the retina, the convex lens reduces the divergence of the rays so that the eye lens can focus them exactly on the retina. In this way, the convex lens enables a long-sighted person to see nearby objects clearly. 38. Compare the use of spectacles and the use of contact lenses to correct visual defects. Ans:- Spectacles are worn outside the eye and are easy to use, durable, and require little cleaning or maintenance, but they can be bulky, may limit side vision, and can be uncomfortable for some people. Contact lenses, on the other hand, sit directly on the cornea and provide a wider field of view, better cosmetic appearance, and more natural vision, but they require careful cleaning, proper handling, and can cause irritation or infection if not used hygienically. 39.
